samples.summary: On a PAGED PR — the stated primary use case — the verb works at most once, and its report/advice are then wrong
samples.evidence: agent-fix.yml's header and docs/design/harness-engineering.md (Phase 30) both say the main reason to reach for `@claude fix` is "a PR the loop gave up on", and that the verb deliberately leaves the paged latch in place. But `.github/workflows/agent-review-panel.yml`'s `gate` job flips `managed = false` when it sees the `<!-- agent-review-paged -->` latch (lines 220-243), so the panel never runs again on a paged PR. Consequences on exactly those PRs: (1) the fix agent's push produces no new panel round, so the `fix-report.mjs read` → `--fix-reports` → adjudication loop this PR adds is inert there; (2) the pushed commit moves the head, so `fix-eligible.mjs` finds no lens check runs on the new head and every subsequent `@claude fix` is permanently refused; (3) the refusal text ("wait for CI to finish and the next panel round to post its verdict", "comment **`@claude loop`** to opt it in") and the agent prompt's "Pushing re-runs CI and a fresh review panel" are both false there — the correct advice would be `@claude rerun`, which clears the latch. Nothing in the design doc's "Not yet built" section records this limitation.

samples.summary: Design doc asserts an on-demand fix is outside MAX_REVIEW_ROUNDS, but the round counter counts the commit it pushes
samples.evidence: The new Phase 30 section states "`MAX_REVIEW_ROUNDS` still counts only autonomous rounds; an on-demand fix is deliberately outside that budget". `scripts/agent/rounds.mjs::fixAttemptCommits` (used by `countFailedReviewRounds`, which review-round-guard.mjs compares against MAX_REVIEW_ROUNDS) counts every single-parent commit carrying failing `agent-review-*` runs after the first verdict, with no attribution to who authored it. An on-demand fix commit that still fails the panel therefore consumes a round of the autonomous budget, contradicting the documented property (and the workflow header's framing of the verb as not touching the round budget).

samples.summary: fix-report.mjs re-implements rebuttal.mjs's hidden-comment codec instead of reusing/extracting it — and the copies have already diverged
samples.evidence: scripts/agent/rebuttal.mjs already provides the same pattern: `REBUTTAL_MARKER` (l.54), `serializeRebuttal` (l.82, `${MARKER}${JSON.stringify(payload)} -->`), `parseRebuttalComment` (l.110, the identical non-greedy `([\s\S]*?) -->` regex), `collectRebuttals` (l.139), `readRebuttals` (l.374, same `--paginate issues/{pr}/comments` call), plus its own local `gh`. fix-report.mjs duplicates all six, and additionally re-declares `parseArgs` even though `scripts/agent/gh-checks.mjs` exports one (fix-brief.mjs and fix-eligible.mjs both import it). The divergence is already real: the `-->`-escaping hazard the new module documents at length applies verbatim to `serializeRebuttal`, whose `claim`/`summary` fields are equally model text copied from findings, and it was fixed only in the new copy. A shared codec (marker + version + serialize/parse/collect/read) would have fixed both — this is the same second-copy rot the PR itself cites as the reason to extract fix-brief.mjs.

samples.summary: `renderClaimForVerifier` is dead code whose docstring claims a consumer that does not exist
samples.evidence: The export is only referenced by fix-report.test.mjs; grep over the repo shows no production import. Its docblock says it is "Kept because the fix BRIEF needs exactly this rendering — telling the next fix round 'you already skipped this one'", but scripts/agent/fix-brief.mjs does not import fix-report.mjs at all and the brief carries no prior-skip context. Either wire the feature or drop the export; as written it ships an unused abstraction with a rationale the code contradicts.

samples.summary: Unrelated pre-existing bug fix (lens stamping on merged findings) bundled into the feature PR
samples.evidence: The `merged` map now stamps `lens` on fresh findings to repair adjudication matching that has been inert since Phase 28. It is a genuine and well-documented fix, but it changes the behaviour of the existing rebuttal→adjudication loop for every PR, independently of `@claude fix`, and it lands inside a PR whose stated scope is the new verb. A separate change would let it be verified (and reverted) on its own.

verdict.reason: All claimed code is present as described. agent-review-panel.yml's gate sets managed=false when it finds the '<!-- agent-review-paged -->' latch (lines 220-244), and every downstream job including review-panel/fix is gated on managed=='true' (line 265), so a paged PR gets no further panel round and no new agent-review-* check runs. fix-eligible.mjs:19-24 (mirrored in agent-fix.yml:5-8 and harness-engineering.md:1727-1730) declares the paged PR the main use case and deliberately leaves the latch in place. Consequences verified: (1) the fix-report -> adjudication path is only consumed by the next panel round (harness-engineering.md:1732-1739), so it is inert there; (2) after the fix push the head moves and fix-eligible.mjs:99-113 hits total===0 and refuses, with the only other review path being read-only (agent-review-on-demand.yml:172 'never checks:write'), so subsequent @claude fix is refused; (3) the refusal text (fix-eligible.mjs:106-113) advises waiting for the next panel round / '@claude loop' and never mentions @claude rerun, the only latch-clearing verb (agent-rerun.yml:1-3,141), while agent-fix.yml:366 and 480-482 assert 'a fresh review panel will run'. The design doc records the paged behavior as a feature (1727-1730) and its MAX_REVIEW_ROUNDS comment (132-134) still describes the pre-latch behavior; nothing records this limitation. This is a spec/design-fit mismatch, not a line-level bug, and I found no guard making it unreachable.

finding.evidence: The new Phase 30 section states "`MAX_REVIEW_ROUNDS` still counts only autonomous rounds; an on-demand fix is deliberately outside that budget". `scripts/agent/rounds.mjs::fixAttemptCommits` (used by `countFailedReviewRounds`, which review-round-guard.mjs compares against MAX_REVIEW_ROUNDS) counts every single-parent commit carrying failing `agent-review-*` runs after the first verdict, with no attribution to who authored it. verdict.reason: The quoted doc claim is present verbatim in the new Phase 30 section (docs/design/harness-engineering.md:1870-1872), and the round counter it describes is provably identity-independent: fixAttemptCommits (scripts/agent/rounds.mjs:174-195) counts any single-parent commit carrying a failing agent-review-* run committed after the first panel verdict, with isSingleParentCommit's own docblock (rounds.mjs:127-137) stating it explicitly is NOT 'was pushed by the fixer'. countFailedReviewRounds (rounds.mjs:202-204) feeds review-round-guard.mjs:209/251-257, which pages at MAX_REVIEW_ROUNDS (agent-review-panel.yml:135,1289). No guard makes this unreachable: the only floor-mover is a human @claude rerun (rounds.mjs:110-125, review-round-guard.mjs:113), and agent-fix.yml writes no such marker anywhere in its fix job (lines 61-280); on a non-paged PR the panel still runs on the fixer's pushed commit, since gate's only skip is the paged latch (agent-review-panel.yml:220-241). So an on-demand @claude fix commit that still fails the panel does consume a round of the autonomous budget, contradicting the documented property (and agent-fix.yml:5-8 / fix-eligible.mjs:21's framing). This sits in the design-fit lane as a design-doc-vs-implementation conformance mismatch in the canonical subsystem doc, not a line-level logic bug.

finding.evidence: scripts/agent/rebuttal.mjs already provides the same pattern: `REBUTTAL_MARKER` (l.54), `serializeRebuttal` (l.82, `${MARKER}${JSON.stringify(payload)} -->`), `parseRebuttalComment` (l.110, the identical non-greedy `([\s\S]*?) -->` regex), `collectRebuttals` (l.139), `readRebuttals` (l.374, same `--paginate issues/{pr}/comments` call), plus its own local `gh`. fix-report.mjs duplicates all six, and additionally re-declares `parseArgs` even though `scripts/agent/gh-checks.mjs` exports one (fix-brief.mjs and fix-eligible.mjs both import it). verdict.reason: Every factual claim verifies. rebuttal.mjs provides REBUTTAL_MARKER (l.54), REBUTTAL_VERSION (l.57), str/trim/defence (l.62-71), serializeRebuttal (l.82, `${MARKER}${JSON.stringify(payload)} -->` at l.96), parseRebuttalComment (l.110-111, non-greedy `([\s\S]*?) -->`), collectRebuttals (l.139), a local gh (l.364), readRebuttals (l.374-376, `repos/{owner}/{repo}/issues/${pr}/comments?per_page=100` with plain --paginate) and a local parseArgs (l.388). fix-report.mjs reproduces all of these with renamed constants: l.38, l.41, l.46-54, l.75/96, l.111-112, l.127, l.415, l.427-429, l.442. The divergence is real: fix-report.mjs:96 escapes the terminator (`-->`) and documents the hazard at l.84-95 and in docs/design/harness-engineering.md:1848-1858, while rebuttal.mjs:96 does not — and rebuttal's claim/summary/evidence are equally verbatim model text taken from findings (cmdPost l.429-437), with the same round-trip refusal (l.441) leading to the same silent "posted nothing". The parseArgs point also holds: gh-checks.mjs:49 exports parseArgs and fix-brief.mjs:33 / fix-eligible.mjs:36 import it, yet fix-report.mjs:442 redeclares its own. I weighed refuting as out-of-scope on the basis that this marker+JSON pattern is a pre-existing repo idiom (metrics.mjs:52/786/790, which both other modules say they "mirror") and that the two record shapes/validation rules genuinely differ, so no whole module was reinvented. But duplication/reuse is squarely in this lens's lane, the duplicated surface is six functions plus shared helpers rather than a one-liner, and the escaping divergence is a concrete, verified instance of the cost — not enough certainty to drop it from the gate.
